title: MCoRe: Multi-Entry Complementary Retrieval with Reflection-Guided Iteration for Multi-Hop QA

problem.claim: Open-domain multi-hop question answering remains challenging because critical bridge evidence may be dispersed across documents and semantic-resolution mismatch can cause retrieval to miss either precise details or necessary context.

contributions.claim: MCoRe is a multi-entry complementary retrieval framework with reflection-guided iteration for multi-hop QA.
It indexes entities, sentences, and summaries at multiple semantic resolutions, links hits to chunk evidence, maps hits to chunks, and fuses them through chunk-level voting.
It identifies missing bridge cues and issues gap-focused follow-up queries when the evidence is insufficient.

author_reported_evidence.claim: MCoRe reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by an average of 6.77 EM points and 8.79 F1 points across three multi-hop QA benchmarks.
On 2Wiki, the reported gains reach up to 12.70 EM points and 14.06 F1 points.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG grounds knowledge-intensive QA in external evidence.
Open-domain multi-hop QA is difficult because evidence is dispersed and retrieval views differ in semantic resolution.
MCoRe combines multi-resolution complementary retrieval with chunk-level evidence fusion.
Reflection-guided iteration issues follow-up queries targeting missing bridge cues.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across three benchmarks, including 2Wiki.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three benchmarks beyond naming 2Wiki.
The abstract does not provide baseline identities, ablations, implementation details, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
